repository.name: gothinkster/golang-gin-realworld-example-app
repository.workload: Change-scoped review of a real, merged pull request: "perf: optimize database queries to eliminate N+1 problems" (PR #49). Not a full-repository review — see docs/evaluation.md §3.6 for the scope this was analyzed under (the diff's five changed files plus their direct callers).

annotation.notes: Retro-annotated from docs/evaluation.md §3.6. This is the ground truth for a CHANGE-SCOPED review of one specific PR, not a full-repository review — compare against a review run with mode=change-scoped against this diff, not against a full review. commit is the PR's merge commit, not pinned in the original review beyond fetching the .diff via GitHub's API; pin the real SHA before scoring an actual run. The point of this file is specifically to test the change-scoped mode's "sits directly adjacent to" rule (SKILL.md §Modes) and its crediting-fixes rule (methodology/change-scoped.md §2) together: the diff correctly fixes half of a two-part problem, and a change-scoped review has to credit that fix while still catching the untouched, structurally identical other half one call deeper in a file the diff already had open.

expected.mechanism: The diff restructures ArticleUserSerializer.Response() (called from inside the loop this diff modifies) but does not touch what that method calls next: ProfileSerializer.Response() -> isFollowing(), which issues its own per-article query. This is the same N+1 shape the diff's own title ("eliminate N+1 problems", plural) targets, one call deeper, in a file the diff already had open. A change-scoped review that only checks whether the diff does what its commit message claims would miss this; SKILL.md's "sits directly adjacent to" language is what requires checking it.

forbidden.why_not: The diff adds BatchGetFavoriteCounts and BatchGetFavoriteStatus and a new ResponseWithPreloaded serializer method, restructuring ArticlesSerializer.Response() to call the batch functions once before its loop rather than per article inside it. This converts the query count from 1+2n to a fixed 3 regardless of page size. The favorites-count N+1 no longer exists in the code this diff produces; reporting it as a live finding would be scoring the pre-diff code, not the change under review. A change-scoped review must credit this as a real, verified fix (methodology/change-scoped.md §2), not re-flag it.
